messages:
dmitri: Heads up — since last night’s driver+kernel roll we’re seeing a lot of jobs degrade to NCCL socket fallback on h100/a100 mixed pools. Throughput down ~3-4x on multi-gpu training runs.
megan: ugh, saw an alert graph too. Is this the 535.75 + kernel 6.5 deploy?
 dmitri: yes. Deploy-bot shows the nodepool bump completed at 02:15 UTC. failures cluster around nodes that have mixed HW (H100 + A100) and different driver micro-versions (535.75 vs 535.62) — nvlink detection looks flaky.
 alex: can you paste the nccl logs from a failing run?
 dmitri: here’s a snippet from the job that regressed:
 ```
[0] NCCL WARN NET/Socket : Unable to create listener on 10.10.8.23:0 - Address family not supported by protocol
[1] NCCL INFO P2P : P2P level falling back to NET from SHM on pair h100-1 <-> a100-3
[2] NCCL WARN TOPO : NVLink peer detection returned empty linkset for GPU(0)
[3] NCCL INFO SOCKET : Using interface eth0, ip 10.10.8.23
```
 jia: that first line looks like an AF_INET6 vs AF_INET mismatch in the socket creation path — maybe kernel changed behavior for bind() on dual-stack?
 megan: any recent sysctl or iptables changes rolled with the kernel?
 dmitri: no iptables changes. We did enable a new IOMMU flag in the kernel config for the build that landed.
 sara: quick check — are nv_peer_mem and nvidia_uvm modules loaded properly on the affected nodes?
 dmitri: nv_peer_mem missing on a few nodes, uvm present. dmesg shows: 
 ```
[  123.456] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and required key missing - tainting kernel
[  123.460] nvidia_uvm: loaded
[  123.462] nv_peer_mem: Module not found
```
 alex: if nv_peer_mem is missing, SHM p2p may be disabled and NCCL falls back to sockets. Why would nv_peer_mem not be present on some nodes? different package builds?
 megan: packaging difference — the node image builder had a kernel-module blacklist step for some SKUs to speed boot. maybe accidentally blacklisted nv_peer_mem for older A100 AMIs.
 deploy-bot: @channel rollout: nodepool/gpu-mixed updated to kernel-6.5.3-driver-535.75 at 02:15 UTC (staggered).
 jia: workaround options: 1) force NCCL to prefer SHM if available with NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=2 or similar, 2) set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to the correct fastpath iface to avoid socket bind oddities, 3) revert the nodepool image for affected SKUs.
 sara: testing suggestion — on a failing node try: `modprobe nv_peer_mem` and rerun a short nccl test (nccl_all_reduce). If modprobe errors, capture `dmesg` and `lsmod`.
 dmitri: tried modprobe on a failed node — returns "module not found". The kernel packaging didn't include the third-party nv_peer_mem module for that AMI variant.
 megan: ugly. For immediate mitigation we could pin affected services to dedicated H100-only pools (where modules were included) and roll back the mixed pool. Cost hit but stabilizes latency.
 alex: also consider a soft fallback: set env `NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=0` and `NCCL_SOCKET_CROSSNET_DISABLE=1`? (testing only).
 jia: careful with envs — some of those aren’t universally supported across NCCL versions. Recommend running a small 2-node smoke test after changing envs.
 sara: ops playbook step: identify nodes missing nv_peer_mem: `for n in $(nodes); do ssh $n lsmod | grep nv_peer_mem || echo $n; done` then add to remediation group.
 dmitri: I started a remediation group and tagged nodes in the infra dashboard. Also added a grafana panel for % jobs using socket fallback by pool.
 megan: long term: we need image-variant parity checks in the pipeline. The node image builder should emit a manifest of kernel modules and we gate rollouts if key modules differ across SKUs.
 alex: +1. Also add an automated smoke that runs nccl peer-detect after image bake.
 deploy-bot: incident created INC-2026-3489: "NCCL P2P socket fallback after kernel/driver rollout" — assigned to eng-infra oncall.
 dmitri: assigning to oncall now. I’ll coordinate rollback plan if remediation takes >2h.
 megan: quick question — did anyone see any other odd logs like "Address family not supported by protocol" across other subsystems?
 jia: saw a couple of kube-proxy warnings around dual-stack endpoints returning unexpected families, might be related.
 sara: for immediate triage I’ll collect a list of affected nodes, module manifests, and the exact package diffs between the h100 and a100 images.
 dmitri: thanks — I’ll pause new schedule-heavy jobs on the mixed pools and move critical runs to H100-only for now. :thumbsup:
 megan: keep updates in this thread and add a short postmortem doc once we have root cause.
 alex: if we end up reverting, coordinate with billing to track cost delta from moving to H100-only.
 dmitri: noted.
 sara: tagging infra-sre for visibility :eyes:
 dmitri: (added) rolling log: will update every 15m.
